newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's CANTV says labor talks going fine.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's CANTV says labor talks going fine.

text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV said Thursday scheduled talks with workers over pay contracts were "advancing normally" and that strike threats raised by unions Wednesday were not justified.

"As 60 percent of the contracts have been agreed, strike action is not justified and would only delay the concluding of accords that guarantee adequate workers' compensation," CANTV said in a press release.
The Federation of Telecommunication Workers (Fetratel), which groups the 29 unions working in CANTV, said Wednesday it might strike if management did not agree to wage demands.
But CANTV said as Fetratel had already agreed over half the salary schedules for 1997 and 1998, "It would be premature to have these talks stall due to strike actions."

CANTV said average salary increases for the coming year, including bonuses, totaled 34 percent with another 65 percent increase penciled in for 1998. Analysts estimate that inflation, which topped 100 percent last year, will reach some 35 percent in 1997.
